title: The Fellah and His Wicked Wife (മലയാളം)
summary: In a quiet village along the Nile lived an honest, hardworking fellah (farmer) named Mas'ud. While plowing his master's field one morning... [ML]
keywords: the fellah and his wicked wife
full_text:
In a quiet village along the Nile lived an honest, hardworking fellah (farmer) named Mas'ud. While plowing his master's field one morning, his plowshare struck a buried earthenware pot filled with ancient Roman gold coins.

Being a man of absolute integrity, Mas'ud did not steal the gold. He carried it straight to the village headman, saying:
'This gold was found in the field of our neighbor, Sheikh Omar; it belongs to him according to law.'

However, Mas'ud's wife, a greedy and discontented woman named Bahija, was furious with him:
'Fool! Thou hadst enough gold to buy ten houses, and thou gavest it away to a rich sheikh! I will have my share, or I will ruin thee!'

That night, Bahija slipped into the headman's granary, stole the pot of gold, hid it in a dry well behind their barn, and substituted a pot filled with dead hornets.
The next morning, she went before the village magistrate, falsely accusing her husband of hiding the real treasure:
'My husband is a liar! He gave you hornets and kept the gold for himself!'

The magistrate, accompanied by the village elders, went to the granary and opened the pot. To Bahija's horror, when the lid was removed, a swarm of stinging hornets flew out, attacking only Bahija, stinging her face and arms until she shrieked and leaped into the irrigation ditch!

Meanwhile, sheep dogs digging near the dry well unearthed the stolen pot of gold.
The magistrate examined the evidence: Mas'ud's honest hands, Bahija's deceit, and the recovered coins.
Sheikh Omar, touched by Mas'ud's steadfast integrity throughout the ordeal, rewarded the honest fellah with half the treasure, a permanent title to five acres of fertile land, and cattle.

Bahija, disgraced by her own malicious deceit, was banished from the village councils, while Mas'ud lived in prosperous peace, celebrated by all the peasants as a shining example of unbending honesty.
moral: Contentment and honesty preserve a home, while deceitful greed brings ruin upon the treacherous. [ML]
